tasks.title: Create the add/list/done/remove command dispatcher with tests
tasks.description: Create src/cli.js exporting run(argv, options): a command dispatcher for add/list/done/remove that takes the store path and output sinks as arguments and returns an exit code. This is the core that both bin/todo.js and the tests drive.

context.reason: Provides loadTodos, saveTodos and nextId that run() dispatches through
Existing node:test and node:assert/strict conventions to mirror in test/cli.test.js

edits.change:
Write an ES module exporting a single named function `run(argv, options)`.

`argv` is the argument array after the script path, e.g. `['add', 'buy milk']`. `options` has two required properties: `filePath` (string, the JSON store location) and `io` (an object with `out(line)` and `err(line)`, used instead of the real streams so tests can capture output). Write output only through io and take the store path only from options.filePath.

Dispatch on `argv[0]`:

- `add`: the text is `argv.slice(1).join(' ')`. If it is empty or whitespace-only, write `Usage: todo add <text>` to io.err and return 1. Otherwise loadTodos, push `{ id: nextId(todos), text, done: false }`, saveTodos, write `Added <id>` to io.out, return 0.
- `list`: loadTodos, drop every todo whose `done` is true when `argv.includes('--pending')`, sort ascending by numeric id. If nothing remains write `No todos.` to io.out and return 0. Otherwise write one line per todo: a done todo is prefixed with `✓ ` and a pending todo with two spaces, followed by `[<id>] <text>`. Return 0.
- `done`: id is `Number(argv[2])`. If it is not a positive integer write `Usage: todo done <id>` to io.err and return 1. Otherwise loadTodos, find the todo with that id, set `done` to true, saveTodos, return 0; if no todo has that id write `No todo with id <id>.` to io.err and return 1.
- `remove`: id is `Number(argv[2])`, validated the same way with usage `Usage: todo remove <id>`. Load todos and filter out the matching one; if nothing matched write `No todo with id <id>.` to io.err and return 1, otherwise saveTodos and return 0.
- Anything else, including an empty argv and `--help`/`-h`: write this usage block to io.err, one line per io.err call, and return 1:

Usage:
  todo add <text>       Add a todo
  todo list [--pending]  List todos; --pending hides completed ones
  todo done <id>        Mark a todo as done
  todo remove <id>      Delete a todo

Each io.out/io.err call receives one complete line with NO trailing newline.

tasks.notes: Document only project-relative paths; this tool stores its JSON in the working directory, not in a user profile directory.

contracts.statement: A todo record is the object { id: number, text: string, done: boolean }. `id` is a positive integer assigned by nextId() as max(existing numeric ids) + 1, starting at 1 for an empty list, and never reused after remove(). The store file is JSON: a top-level array of todo records, pretty-printed with 2-space indentation and a trailing newline.

Every path this tool touches is project-relative. The store path is always supplied by the caller as an argument: src/store.js and src/cli.js must derive nothing from the environment, the operating system or a user profile directory. Only bin/todo.js chooses a default, and that default is `.todos.json` in the current working directory, overridden by process.env.TODO_FILE when that variable is set and non-empty.

src/cli.js exports exactly one named function, run(argv, options), where argv is the argument array after the script path and options is { filePath: string, io: { out(line: string): void, err(line: string): void } }. run() returns a number (0 on success, 1 on a usage error or an unknown id) and writes output only through options.io; it never writes to process.stdout or process.stderr. Every line passed to io.out or io.err is a complete line with no trailing newline, so the caller appends one.
